boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Mississippi traditions, from game-day rituals to recurring student events.

cards.title: Answer the Hotty Toddy call
cards.subtitle: University-wide cheer and greeting
cards.notes: Learn the call-and-response before a game or campus event, then join only when the crowd starts it.
cards.short_summary: Ole Miss identifies Hotty Toddy as its cheer, rallying cry and shared greeting.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes Hotty Toddy as a feeling, an ideal, a fight song, a rallying cry and a handshake.
cards.source_title: Campus Culture and Traditions | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: Listen for the “Are you ready?” prompt; participation is optional.

cards.title: Stand for the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: Athletic and ceremonial occasions
cards.notes: When the Alma Mater is played, stand if able, remove hats or caps, and follow the university’s cue to sing.
cards.short_summary: The 1925 Alma Mater remains part of athletic events, commencement and reunions.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss says its Alma Mater was written in 1925 and is sung and played at athletic events, commencement, reunions and other ceremonies.
cards.source_title: Campus Culture and Traditions | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: The university asks attendees to stand if able and remove hats or caps.

cards.title: Line the Walk of Champions
cards.subtitle: The Grove to Vaught-Hemingway Stadium
cards.notes: Arrive ahead of a home football game and watch from the route as the team makes its scheduled stadium walk.
cards.short_summary: The football team’s pregame walk begins beneath the arch on the east side of the Grove.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss states that the team begins its walk to the stadium at the Walk of Champions arch two hours and 15 minutes before every home game.
cards.source_title: Campus Culture and Traditions | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: Occurs before home football games; check the official game schedule for kickoff timing.

cards.title: Lock arms at the Vaught
cards.subtitle: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium pre-kickoff ritual
cards.notes: At a home football game, follow the crowd’s lead before kickoff: link arms only with willing neighbors and sway in place.
cards.short_summary: Fans and students link arms and sway before the Rebels take the field.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss documents that students and fans lock arms and sway to “Come With Me” before opening kickoff at home football games.
cards.source_title: Campus Culture and Traditions | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: Only occurs at home football games; respect personal space in crowded seating.

cards.title: Watch the Home Run Showers
cards.subtitle: Swayze Field right-field bleachers
cards.notes: Choose a dry viewing spot if you prefer; the right-field students toss cup contents upward after Ole Miss home runs.
cards.short_summary: A baseball home run prompts a celebratory spray from the right-field bleachers.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss says students beyond the right-field fence throw what is in their cups into the air whenever the Rebels hit a home run.
cards.source_title: Campus Culture and Traditions | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: Watch rather than stand in the splash zone; admission policies vary by game.

cards.title: Run the field with Rebel Run
cards.subtitle: First-year student football-game tradition
cards.notes: If you are eligible, register through Student Activities Association instructions and follow staff directions for the field run.
cards.short_summary: First-year students take the field before a football game as part of an Ole Miss tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss Student Activities Association identifies Rebel Run as a campus tradition in which first-year students take the field before a football game.
cards.access_notes: Participation is for eligible first-year students and is directed by event staff.

cards.title: See Parade of Beauties
cards.subtitle: Student Activities Association pageant tradition
cards.notes: Check Student Activities Association announcements for the next event, then attend as a spectator and support participants respectfully.
cards.short_summary: This longstanding pageant names one student Ole Miss Most Beautiful.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss Student Activities Association calls Parade of Beauties a longstanding tradition that names an Ole Miss Most Beautiful winner.
cards.access_notes: Event timing and attendance details are announced by Student Activities Association.

cards.title: Follow Homecoming Week to court crowning
cards.subtitle: Student Activities Association annual programming
cards.notes: Use the Student Activities Association schedule to pick an activity, then follow the week through the Saturday court crowning.
cards.short_summary: Ole Miss Homecoming Week culminates in crowning the Homecoming Court on Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss Student Activities Association says Fall Homecoming Week culminates with the crowning of the Homecoming Court on Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Consult Student Activities Association for the current week’s activities and locations.

cards.entity_name: Pride of the South Pre-Game Routine
cards.title: Catch the Pride’s Grove pregame
cards.subtitle: Grove Stage before home football games
cards.notes: Get to the Grove Stage before the game to hear the band’s traditional pre-game routine before heading toward the stadium.
cards.short_summary: The Pride of the South performs a traditional routine at the Grove Stage before every home game.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss states that before every home game, the Pride of the South gathers at the Grove Stage and performs its traditional pre-game routine.
cards.source_title: Campus Culture and Traditions | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: Occurs before home football games; allow time for game-day pedestrian traffic.

cards.title: Visit the Grove on game day
cards.subtitle: The Grove football-weekend gathering
cards.notes: Walk the Grove on a home-game Saturday, keep paths clear, and enjoy the public game-day atmosphere without assuming an invitation to tents.
cards.short_summary: The Grove has hosted Ole Miss football tailgating since the 1950s.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss’s institutional repository states that the Grove became the home for Ole Miss tailgating during the 1950s.
cards.source_title: The Grove | University of Mississippi eGrove
cards.access_notes: Game-day access and tent rules are set by the university and athletics event guidance.
